chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

A supplication to be recited at the end of every prayer you pray. If there is an illness in you from disease and pain, so when you complete your prayer, wipe your hand upon the place of your prostration from the ground, and supplicate with this supplication, and pass your hand over the place of your pain seven times, saying.

O the One Who Compressed the earth upon the water, and Filled the atmosphere with the sky, and Chose for Himself the best of the Names! Send Blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and do such and such with me, and Grace me with such and such, and Grant me good health from such and such (pain).
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for healing recited after prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication highlights the Shia practice of utilizing the physical residue of prostration (turab) as a medium for divine healing, linking the humility of prayer with tangible relief. The invocation emphasizes God's creative power over the elements—earth, water, and air—before petitioning for specific needs, reflecting the tradition of combining theological affirmation with personal du'a. This ritual underscores the belief in the spiritual efficacy of post-prayer acts and the intercessory nature of divine names.
